agent_relevance.agent_integration_path: Among the more agent-ready surfaces in this cohort: a pip-installable CLI, an API token and base URL, and seven agent skills the documentation says load into Claude Code or Codex so an agent can call search-papers and synthesise from saved artifacts. No MCP server is documented. Behaviourally testable via the CLI once credentials are issued.

hlido_opinion.headline: A graph-backed research platform claiming the largest structured science knowledge graph, with agent skills that load into Claude Code and Codex — scale unverified by us.
hlido_opinion.body: Hlido's automated public-surface checks recorded no passes on this run even though the page rendered and was captured in full, so the score reflects what our checks could VERIFY, not a judgement that the product is weak. Read the score as low confidence pending a re-test, and the notes below as what the captured surface says about itself. SciAtlas positions itself as infrastructure for automated science rather than another literature search box, and the captured surface is specific enough to argue with. It claims 43M+ papers across 26 disciplines, 157M entity nodes and 3B relation edges, a published schema of 9 entity types and 12 relation types (paper, author, institution, topic, keyword, source, domain, field, subfield), and a retrieval approach it calls tri-path collaborative recall with graph re-ranking — explicitly framed as moving from surface semantic matching toward topological reasoning. The three documented workflows are the right ones for the claim: evidence-grounded literature review with thematic clustering and gap analysis, idea grounding and evaluation with rubric-based critique and go/revise/no-go recommendations, and cross-disciplinary idea generation with KG evidence chains and minimal validation experiments. That last one is where a knowledge graph genuinely beats a vector index, and the discipline mix published on the page (Medicine 18.6%, Social Sciences 10.7%, Engineering 9.4%) is an unusually checkable detail. For an agent ecosystem the important part is the integration path: a pip-installable CLI, an API token, and seven agent skills the docs say load into Claude Code or Codex so an agent can run search-papers, inspect saved artifacts and synthesise downstream — this is built to be driven, not just read. The caution is proportional to the claim: 'the largest structured scientific knowledge graph available' is a superlative with no published comparison or coverage method, the service runs on a university-affiliated host, and nothing on the page speaks to availability or rate limits.

tier_rationale: FADING (50) is a confidence verdict, not a quality one: every required public-surface check failed on this run, so the graph scale, the retrieval method, the CLI and the agent skills are all unconfirmed by us. A superlative coverage claim with no published method is exactly what a register must decline to credit until measured, and a re-test is queued. It is not lower because the captured surface is detailed, publishes a real schema and a per-discipline breakdown, and documents a concrete install path a user can falsify.
what_it_does_well: Publishes an actual graph schema (9 entity types, 12 relation types) rather than a vague 'knowledge graph' claim
Discipline coverage is given as a checkable percentage breakdown across 26 fields
Three documented workflows map to real research tasks, including rubric-based go/revise/no-go idea evaluation
Cross-disciplinary concept fusion is a use case a graph genuinely serves better than a vector index
Designed to be agent-driven: pip-installable CLI, API token, and skills that load into Claude Code or Codex
States that outputs carry KG evidence chains — the right posture for research tooling
what_it_fails_at: All required public-surface checks failed on this run — the scale and method claims are unverified by us
'Largest structured scientific knowledge graph available' is a superlative with no published comparison or method
No availability, rate-limit or uptime commitment for a service research workflows would depend on
Hosted on a university-affiliated domain with no stated operational or funding continuity
No pricing or access terms published, so cost of dependence is unknown
No independent evaluation of retrieval quality against the vector-search baseline it claims to beat
best_for: Researchers doing cross-disciplinary literature work where graph traversal beats keyword or vector search
Agent-driven research pipelines that can consume the CLI and agent skills
Teams needing evidence chains attached to generated literature reviews
Idea-stage evaluation where novelty and prior-art grounding matter
not_recommended_for: Production workflows needing an availability guarantee (none is published)
Anyone who needs the coverage superlative verified before relying on it
Simple single-paper lookups — the graph machinery is overhead for that
Commercial use without first clarifying access terms, which are not on the public surface
red_flags: Claims 'the largest structured scientific knowledge graph available' with no published comparison or coverage method — an unverifiable superlative
All required public-surface checks failed on this run while the page rendered fully — the score reflects unverified claims, not measured weakness; a re-test is queued

compared_to.verdict_diff: Elicit is a mature, operated research assistant with a clear product and pricing. SciAtlas offers graph traversal and an agent-drivable CLI with no stated operational commitment. Elicit when you need the service to be there tomorrow; SciAtlas when cross-disciplinary graph structure is the requirement.

Perplexity answers questions with web citations across everything. SciAtlas is scoped to structured scientific literature with a traversable graph and method lineages. Perplexity for breadth and immediacy; SciAtlas for depth within science.

LlamaIndex is the toolkit for building your own retrieval over your own corpus. SciAtlas is a pre-built graph over published science. Build with LlamaIndex if the corpus is yours; use SciAtlas if the corpus is the literature.
